goal: Build multidimensional senior-year trajectory analysis for students, parents and teacher-facing shares without turning the product into a generic score table.
productPrinciple: 再回到具体考试和分数核对
nonGoals: No high-stakes prediction of Gaokao score or admission outcome.
No radar chart as the primary comparison UI.
No teacher account system in v0.3.0; teacher use is a privacy-scoped share preset.
No third-party analytics or new paid storage dependency.

stages.name: release safety and weak-network recovery
acceptance: All work stays on this PR branch until every stage is green.
This checkpoint and PR body remain authoritative after interruption.
Every material commit updates this checkpoint status before release.
Do not infer completed work from chat history; verify branch diff, tests and checkpoint.
Do not use destructive reset/checkout over unverified work.
No broad subtree MutationObserver regression; exam entry responsiveness remains protected.

stages.name: single-subject historical trajectory
acceptance: Six subjects each have a history view across exams.
Show score trajectory, school rank/percentile trajectory and class rank trajectory when available.
If participant count is absent, degrade to rank-only and never invent percentile.
Summarize latest-vs-previous and recent 3-6 comparable exams.
Explain that score changes across different exam difficulty are not equivalent to relative-position changes.
PC and Android both support subject switching without hover-only behavior.

stages.name: six-subject change map
acceptance: Compare all six subjects by current relative position, direction and stability.
Prefer school percentile/rank, then class rank, then score-only with explicit caveat.
Identify primary contributors moving forward and subjects worth attention without alarmist language.
Do not put six unreadable lines or a radar chart in the primary UI.

stages.name: multidimensional trajectory sharing
acceptance: Trajectory share contains Overview, Subject, Six-subject comparison and Exam timeline dimensions.
Existing single-exam share remains pinned to the selected exam.
Shared subject view can browse each subject's historical score/rank/percentile data.
Shared six-subject comparison is readable on phone and desktop.
Existing clickable/touch exam timeline remains available and current/past states stay distinct.
Share projection remains allow-listed; private notes never leak.

stages.name: exam comparability metadata
acceptance: Exam data supports an optional comparison series/group and comparison level/type metadata without breaking schema-v1 records.
Analysis prefers same comparison series when enough points exist.
Cross-series or mixed-scope trends display a clear comparability caveat instead of overclaiming.
Old exams with no comparability metadata continue to render and analyze conservatively.

stages.name: student-parent-teacher reading perspectives
acceptance: Student copy emphasizes where I am and which subject is changing.
Parent copy emphasizes what changed and what is worth attention, avoiding panic wording.
Teacher share preset exposes academic trajectory fields only and never account/family/private-note data.
Perspectives are display/share presets over one data model, not duplicated records.

stages.name: release gate
acceptance: Version is 0.3.0 across package, lockfile and Worker APP_VERSION.
npm run verify passes on final PR head.
Regression tests cover rank-only data, multi-exam subject comparison, sharing privacy, comparability fallbacks, Android-friendly interaction and observer safety.
PR is merged only with expected_head_sha after final CI is green.
main CI passes.
Cloudflare deploy checks out the exact tested SHA.
Production /api/health attests appVersion=0.3.0 before declaring complete.

restartProtocol: 1. Fetch current main SHA and this branch head; never assume chat-state is current.
2. Read this checkpoint and PR body completely.
3. Inspect PR changed files/diff and latest CI before changing code.
4. Treat only committed code + passing tests as completed; never mark a stage complete from prose alone.
5. Resume the first stage whose status is not completed, preserving already-committed work.
6. If main advanced, compare/reconcile deliberately; do not force-reset the feature branch.
7. Update this checkpoint after each completed stage and before final merge.
